messages.subject: Adobe Lightroom experience
parts:
Hello,

does anybody have experience with tagging in adobe lightroom? Maybe even tagging for Random Encounter Model? I want to tag species and number of individuals seen.

I have difficulties in understanding the right workflow. There are several separate fields in the tab 'Metadata', like 'file name', 'contact', 'content', 'image' etc.
Which tag field should I use?
Do I use only one field?
How do I separate tags?
Are the tags saved automatically onto the files or do I have to export all the files?

Thank you in advance,
Tobias

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Adobe Lightroom experience
parts:
Hi Tobias,

sorry, I missed your email - Google sometimes puts emails from the group into the spam folder.

Did you read vignette 2?

https://jniedballa.github.io/camtrapR/articles/camtrapr2.html

The section on metadata tagging would be relevant for you. You can create whatever tags you want (in digiKam it's under Captions > Tags), e.g. species, number of individuals, distance, speed, or whatever is relevant for you. These information are stored in the "HierarchicalSubject" tag, from where camtrapR can read them (via Exiftool).

I have no experience with lightroom, but the metadata you mentioned are likely the EXIF metadata which you don't want to change.

The suggested workflow uses digiKam (because free and open source, and good). I expect the workflows to be quite similar, and many years ago the workflow was compatible with tags from Adobe Bridge. I can't guarantee it works though.

There are a few tagged sample images in camtrapR. You can find them via:

wd_images_ID_species_tagged <- system.file("pictures/sample_images_species_tag",
                                           package = "camtrapR")

Load these into Lightroom (copy them somewhere else first) and the (species) tags should hopefully be read out. Following that example, add some more tags and see if recordTable can read them out.

Please let us know if it works or if you have more questions. Would be good to have some feedback from a Lightroom user.

Best,

Jürgen
